auditFocus: field-level @Autowired injection instead of constructor injection with final fields (Java) or val properties (Kotlin)
a public method calling another @Transactional method on `this` within the same class, relying on the self-invocation proxy that Spring's AOP-based transaction management cannot intercept
a controller/service returning a JPA entity directly instead of a DTO, leaking persistence internals and lazy-loading traps across the API boundary
a lazy-loaded association accessed in a loop with no @EntityGraph/fetch join, producing an N+1 query pattern
a request DTO with no Bean Validation (jakarta.validation) annotations, or a controller that trusts unvalidated input
a SecurityFilterChain/authorization rule that is overly permissive, or CSRF disabled on a session-based (cookie-authenticated) endpoint with no compensating control
buildCommands: ./gradlew build (or mvn verify, matching the project's build tool)
./gradlew check (or the project's configured lint/static-analysis task, when configured)
fixGuardrails: Never switch field @Autowired injection back in to work around a wiring error instead of fixing the constructor/bean definition.
Never widen a SecurityFilterChain rule (e.g. permitAll on a protected path) just to make a 403 disappear.
Never disable a failing test or a Bean Validation constraint to reach a green build.
Never add a broad exception handler that swallows the root cause instead of fixing it.
